concepts.definition: Equity or warrant incentives offered to customers can alter effective pricing, acquisition economics and the distribution of business risk.
concepts.keyQuestion: How much of this 'core' revenue is an add-back of equity handed to the customer?
concepts.use_when: How much of this 'core' revenue is an add-back of equity handed to the customer?
concepts.evidence: Value contractual incentives consistently and compare retention and purchases after subsidies expire.
concepts.falsifier: Unsubsidized repeat demand weakens a thesis that the incentive alone supports the relationship.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Noncash incentives still have an economic cost; avoid double counting dilution and expense adjustments.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 167; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: The Vertical Wrapper (Paying to Enter the Build)

concepts.name: Group Value-Source Migration
concepts.definition: A diversified group's source of value can shift between businesses even while aggregate results conceal the transition.
concepts.keyQuestion: Which entity in this group is now the engine, and which is being carried by a mark on it?
concepts.use_when: Which entity in this group is now the engine, and which is being carried by a mark on it?
concepts.evidence: Bridge segment cash flows, capital requirements and risk to group valuation over time.
concepts.falsifier: Stable segment contributions weaken a proposed migration of the value center.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Intersegment transactions and shared costs need reconciliation.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 168; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Credit-Supported Asset Financing
concepts.definition: Long-lived asset financing often depends on the credit quality and tenor of customers, sponsors or other contractual supporters.
concepts.keyQuestion: Which rating is really being pledged here, through which seam would it leak, and who is assumed to take the paper out?
concepts.use_when: Which rating is really being pledged here, through which seam would it leak, and who is assumed to take the paper out?
concepts.evidence: Match asset life and five listed tenor categories with funding maturities, support and refinancing conditions.
concepts.falsifier: Weak or short-lived credit support can break financing even when the asset has demand.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: The source says four tenors but lists five; support reduces some risks without eliminating them.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 170; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Merchant and Captive Measurement Boundary
concepts.definition: Separate open-market transactions from internal production when estimating market size, shares and investment returns.
concepts.keyQuestion: Which channels of this build are invisible to the public numbers, and how much does that bias the read?
concepts.use_when: Which channels of this build are invisible to the public numbers, and how much does that bias the read?
concepts.evidence: Reconcile merchant revenue, captive capacity, internal transfers and final-customer spending.
concepts.falsifier: A stable reconciled boundary can overturn a growth claim driven only by reclassification.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Use different totals for different questions and never silently add them.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 172; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: The Rack Ate a Layer (The Invisible Channels)

concepts.name: AI Cost Incidence in Software
concepts.definition: AI can add workload-sensitive production costs to software and redistribute margin pressure through the product and supplier stack.
concepts.keyQuestion: Where in this software P&L is the inference bill landing, and what lever pulls the margin back?
concepts.use_when: Where in this software P&L is the inference bill landing, and what lever pulls the margin back?
concepts.evidence: Measure inference, tools, support, retries and review cost by user and accepted outcome.
concepts.falsifier: Low or declining incremental cost relative to realized value weakens a margin-compression thesis.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Software already had nonzero costs; AI cost structure varies by architecture and usage.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 174; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: Software Acquires a Cost of Goods

concepts.name: Discovery Channel Erosion
concepts.definition: A change in how users discover answers can reduce or redirect referrals and monetization for businesses dependent on the prior channel.
concepts.keyQuestion: Is this revenue being generated by the funnel or by squeezing a base the funnel stopped refilling?
concepts.use_when: Is this revenue being generated by the funnel or by squeezing a base the funnel stopped refilling?
concepts.evidence: Track task-level impressions, referrals, conversion, direct demand and alternate acquisition routes.
concepts.falsifier: Stable profitable conversion despite fewer visits weakens a revenue-loss inference.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Traffic, qualified demand and revenue are distinct; effects differ by task and segment.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 175; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: The Discovery Tax (The Curse Is in the Funnel)

concepts.name: Information Substitution and Transaction Completion
concepts.definition: An agent may substitute for an informational step without being able or authorized to complete the associated transaction.
concepts.keyQuestion: Can an agent satisfy this demand with a summary, or does something still have to clear?
concepts.use_when: Can an agent satisfy this demand with a summary, or does something still have to clear?
concepts.evidence: Test discovery, interpretation, permission, payment and exception handling separately.
concepts.falsifier: Successful authorized completion can refute a claim that the business controls an indispensable final step.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: A content response is not evidence of execution capability.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 176; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: Content Is Summarizable, Settlement Must Clear

concepts.name: Machine-Access Monetization
concepts.definition: A business may charge for reliable machine access to information, actions or outcomes when those services create measurable value.
concepts.keyQuestion: Has this toll authority secured the position, and is it collecting yet or still carrying the traffic free?
concepts.use_when: Has this toll authority secured the position, and is it collecting yet or still carrying the traffic free?
concepts.evidence: Test paying demand, access rights, substitution, service quality and delivery cost.
concepts.falsifier: Cheap equivalent lawful access or weak willingness to pay undermines the toll thesis.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Technical access control alone does not create a durable rent.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 178; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: The Toll Authority (The Property Line Repriced)

concepts.name: Interface-to-Substrate Transition
concepts.definition: A product can lose control of the user interface yet retain value as the system that performs transactions, enforces rules or stores authoritative state.
concepts.keyQuestion: Has this incumbent conceded the interface, and what is the substrate business worth once it has?
concepts.use_when: Has this incumbent conceded the interface, and what is the substrate business worth once it has?
concepts.evidence: Separate interface usage from backend transaction volume, switching cost and retained economics.
concepts.falsifier: Replaceable backend services with falling retained margin weaken the substrate defense.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Losing the interface may still weaken distribution and bargaining power.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 179; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Segment-Level Substitution
concepts.definition: Technology substitution depends on the task, customer and workflow segment, so aggregate company labels can conceal opposing effects.
concepts.keyQuestion: Which segment inside this total has gone negative, and which agent behaviour explains it?
concepts.use_when: Which segment inside this total has gone negative, and which agent behaviour explains it?
concepts.evidence: Compare adoption, quality, switching and economics by segment.
concepts.falsifier: Uniform effects across well-defined segments weaken the need for a segmented explanation.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Define segments before observing the outcome to reduce convenient reclassification.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 180; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: Substitution Shows Up in the Segments Before the Total

concepts.name: Metric Definition Drift
concepts.definition: A reported metric can change because its counting rule, population or period changed rather than because the underlying business improved.
concepts.keyQuestion: What changed in the definition of this number, and in which quarter did the change arrive?
concepts.use_when: What changed in the definition of this number, and in which quarter did the change arrive?
concepts.evidence: Maintain a definition ledger and recompute comparable series where data permits.
concepts.falsifier: Stable definitions and reconciled denominators support a real change in performance.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: A changed definition can be legitimate; disclose its effect without assuming intent.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 181; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: The Definition Moved With the Number

concepts.name: Earnings per Share Attribution
concepts.definition: Changes in earnings per share can arise from operations, financing, taxes, marks and share-count changes with different durability.
concepts.keyQuestion: How much of this earnings growth is operating, how much is a mark, and how much is a smaller share count bought with debt?
concepts.use_when: How much of this earnings growth is operating, how much is a mark, and how much is a smaller share count bought with debt?
concepts.evidence: Bridge net income and weighted shares to EPS, separating operating and non-operating components.
concepts.falsifier: Stable share count and clean operating improvement weaken a financial-engineering explanation.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Buybacks are not automatically value creating; price paid, financing and alternatives matter.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 182; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Free-Tier Unit Economics
concepts.definition: A free user creates costs and potential future value; evaluate acquisition, conversion, learning and network benefits against actual delivery expense.
concepts.keyQuestion: Is this company's free tier an asset it monetizes elsewhere or a bill it has not yet found a payer for?
concepts.use_when: Is this company's free tier an asset it monetizes elsewhere or a bill it has not yet found a payer for?
concepts.evidence: Measure cohort contribution, conversion, retention, compute and support cost over a stated horizon.
concepts.falsifier: Profitable conversion or network effects can justify a free tier despite positive marginal cost.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Paid-from-day-one is an option, not a universal requirement; web products also had costs.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 186; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: Get Big Fast, Monetize Later vs Paid From Day One
The Free User Is a Cost

applications.name: Free Growth and Paid Entry
applications.definition: Choose free, paid or mixed entry by comparing customer acquisition and learning benefits with actual servicing cost and conversion.
applications.evidence: Model cohort contribution, capacity use, willingness to pay and alternative acquisition paths.
applications.falsifier: Profitable free cohorts undermine a claim that every AI wedge must charge immediately.
applications.limits: Neither web distribution nor AI delivery has a universal marginal-cost law.

concepts.name: Revenue Architecture Comparison
concepts.definition: Compare revenue architectures through consistent payer, unit, cost, distribution, retention, control and capital assumptions.
concepts.keyQuestion: In which column does this business sit on each row, and which two rows changed?
concepts.use_when: In which column does this business sit on each row, and which two rows changed?
concepts.evidence: Populate a common comparison table using the same period and definitions for each architecture.
concepts.falsifier: Unreconciled units or omitted costs make an apparent advantage non-comparable.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: The nine rows are unit of sale, cost of goods, gross margin, price, customer shape, free user, moat, balance sheet and metric; populate observations rather than assuming era-wide economics.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 188; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Information Inputs and Value Appropriation
concepts.definition: Value from widely available informational inputs can accrue to the intermediary that organizes or distributes them; privately generated decision records may create a different opportunity for retained value.
concepts.keyQuestion: Who refined this firm's first barrel, and is the second barrel priced and owned before the first runs out?
concepts.use_when: Who refined this firm's first barrel, and is the second barrel priced and owned before the first runs out?
concepts.evidence: Trace input rights, contributor compensation, traffic or other exchange benefits, intermediary economics and the ownership and substitutability of operating records.
concepts.falsifier: Contributors retaining bargaining power or intermediaries unable to capture incremental value weaken the appropriation thesis.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: The web-history and recursive-data claims are case hypotheses requiring evidence. Decision records are not automatically unique, owned, lawful to reuse or economically valuable.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 189; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: The Data Oil and the Second Barrel
concepts.category: Deployment, product economics and outcomes · Enterprise processes, ownership and procurement

concepts.name: Multi-Axis Routing
concepts.definition: Routing spans model choice, execution stage, hardware, cost, jurisdiction and policy. Choose among feasible allocations using quality, latency, total cost, authority and risk criteria.
concepts.keyQuestion: Where in this stack is the routing decision made, on how many axes, and who owns the rules that make it?
concepts.use_when: Where in this stack is the routing decision made, on how many axes, and who owns the rules that make it?
concepts.evidence: Map the six source dimensions separately from selection criteria, then compare routed outcomes against a fixed-allocation baseline.
concepts.falsifier: A simpler allocation with equivalent accepted quality, compliance and lower overhead weakens the routing advantage.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: The six dimensions are a useful design inventory, not a universal optimization formula; value need not concentrate in the router.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 190; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Routing Across Scales
concepts.definition: Resource-allocation patterns can recur at task, workflow, team and firm levels, but the authority and feedback at each level differ.
concepts.keyQuestion: At which altitude is this router operating, and what does the same pattern look like one rung up and one rung down?
concepts.use_when: At which altitude is this router operating, and what does the same pattern look like one rung up and one rung down?
concepts.evidence: Match the allocation mechanism, decision rights and feedback speed before transferring a routing analogy.
concepts.falsifier: A mismatch in authority or observability invalidates the cross-scale transfer.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: This is a comparative lens, not proof that all scales follow one fractal law.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 191; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Model, Harness and Context Fit
concepts.definition: System performance depends on interactions among the model, orchestration, context, tools and evaluation design.
concepts.keyQuestion: Am I improving the model, or the fit between model, harness, and context, and which one is cheaper to move?
concepts.use_when: Am I improving the model, or the fit between model, harness, and context, and which one is cheaper to move?
concepts.evidence: Test component changes and combinations on representative tasks with equal resource accounting.
concepts.falsifier: No interaction effect or a simpler configuration matching results weakens a co-adaptation thesis.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: A successful benchmark configuration may not generalize to new tasks or releases.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 193; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Cross-Depth Artifact Reuse
concepts.definition: A structured artifact created for retrieval can also support training or model adaptation if its rights, representation and quality permit reuse across those depths.
concepts.keyQuestion: Which artifact built for retrieval is also this firm's training substrate, and does it hold clear title to it?
concepts.use_when: Which artifact built for retrieval is also this firm's training substrate, and does it hold clear title to it?
concepts.evidence: Test a grounding graph or retrieval corpus as adaptation data, measuring transformation effort, held-out performance, provenance and permitted uses.
concepts.falsifier: Large reconstruction cost, rights restrictions or no improvement on fresh tasks weakens the cross-depth reuse claim.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Retrieval suitability does not guarantee training suitability, model ownership or a ready path to a co-designed model.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 195; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Selective Openness
concepts.definition: Opening an interface or complement can increase adoption and demand for a retained junction while leaving selected rules, assets or distribution under the firm's control.
concepts.keyQuestion: Which layer does this actor want open, which does it hold, and what does the roster of absences say?
concepts.use_when: Which layer does this actor want open, which does it hold, and what does the roster of absences say?
concepts.evidence: Map licenses, interoperability and export rights, then measure induced adoption, demand for the retained component, monetization and switching costs.
concepts.falsifier: Open complements that enable substitutes without increasing profitable demand weaken the demand-policy thesis.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Open interfaces, open source and open weights grant different rights; openness need not increase rent capture.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 196; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: Restriction vs Diffusion (Openness as Demand Policy)

applications.name: Openness as a Competitive Boundary
applications.definition: Use a company case to ask which interfaces are opened and which economically important functions remain controlled.
applications.evidence: Verify current product terms, interoperability and switching evidence for the named case.
applications.falsifier: Usable alternatives without dependence challenge the proposed boundary.
applications.limits: The source's Palantir example is a historical illustration, not a verified current company fact.

concepts.name: Capability Absorption Risk
concepts.definition: A feature can lose independent value when an upstream platform incorporates a sufficiently good substitute into an existing distribution channel.
concepts.keyQuestion: Which parts of this product compensate for a temporary gap, and which would the firm still need after the next release?
concepts.use_when: Which parts of this product compensate for a temporary gap, and which would the firm still need after the next release?
concepts.evidence: Compare roadmap evidence, task quality, bundling, customer switching and the product's retained assets.
concepts.falsifier: Persistent willingness to pay for differentiated workflow value weakens the absorption thesis.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: A release announcement does not prove substitution; timing and integration matter.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 198; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
concepts.category: Intelligence systems and architecture · Strategy, competition and value capture

concepts.name: Compute Stage and Workload Economics
concepts.definition: Training, adaptation, prefill, decoding, retrieval and tool execution have different resource profiles and cost drivers.
concepts.keyQuestion: Which stage of the token lifecycle does this cost or moat live in, and does it scale with reasoning?
concepts.use_when: Which stage of the token lifecycle does this cost or moat live in, and does it scale with reasoning?
concepts.evidence: Measure workload-specific throughput, latency, hardware use and cost under comparable service requirements.
concepts.falsifier: Different workload mixes can overturn a claimed hardware or cost advantage.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: No universal decoding ratio or annual cost-decline rate applies to every system.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 199; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: The Three-Stage Token Lifecycle (The Reasoning Tax)

concepts.name: Commercial and Capability Workload Allocation
concepts.definition: Externally sold product workloads and internally consumed capability workloads can compete for a shared substrate; revenue visibility may bias allocation against internal capability.
concepts.keyQuestion: Which workload does this substrate's roadmap bend toward, and what does the bend crowd out?
concepts.use_when: Which workload does this substrate's roadmap bend toward, and what does the bend crowd out?
concepts.evidence: Separate external and internal demand, service requirements, utilization and roadmap decisions; measure which work is delayed and the value it would create.
concepts.falsifier: Balanced allocation and supported internal service levels weaken a merchant-bias diagnosis.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: External work can lose money and internal work can be operational. Volume and burstiness depend on the workload, not its label.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 201; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: Product Workloads vs Capability Workloads (The Inference Cage)

concepts.name: Architecture Specialization Signal
concepts.definition: Specialized architecture may reveal an economically important workload constraint, but its value depends on real utilization and system fit.
concepts.keyQuestion: What does this split confess about the years the line was unified?
concepts.use_when: What does this split confess about the years the line was unified?
concepts.evidence: Compare representative benchmarks, total deployment costs and demand for the specialized function.
concepts.falsifier: A flexible alternative with comparable economics weakens the specialization advantage.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Architecture announcements are evidence of a bet, not proof of a new market regime.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 202; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Iteration Access and Talent Retention
concepts.definition: Access to tools, compute, users and fast feedback can affect expert learning speed and the attractiveness of an organization.
concepts.keyQuestion: What is this lab's queue latency, and who leaves first when it lengthens?
concepts.use_when: What is this lab's queue latency, and who leaves first when it lengthens?
concepts.evidence: Compare time to experiment, feedback quality, autonomy and retention reasons across teams.
concepts.falsifier: Compensation, management or mission explaining departures better weakens the iteration-access hypothesis.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Do not infer individual motives from infrastructure differences alone.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 203; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: The Option to Iterate (Rationing Reprices the Bench)

concepts.name: Semantic Index Control
concepts.definition: A maintained representation of entities, meanings and relationships can become a valuable control point when workflows depend on its accuracy and portability.
concepts.keyQuestion: Who is building the graph over this corpus, from what signal, and who holds it once built?
concepts.use_when: Who is building the graph over this corpus, from what signal, and who holds it once built?
concepts.evidence: Test semantic completeness, maintenance, provenance, query usefulness and export into an alternative runtime.
concepts.falsifier: Cheap reconstruction with equivalent performance weakens a durable-index advantage.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Owning a graph does not by itself create a moat or authority to act.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 204; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
concepts.category: Intelligence systems and architecture · Enterprise processes, ownership and procurement

concepts.name: Four-Plane Intelligence Architecture
concepts.definition: Distinguish application interaction, context and knowledge, execution, and governance to assign responsibilities and locate failure boundaries.
concepts.keyQuestion: What does this agent actually read at the moment of action, and where is the policy enforced if not there?
concepts.use_when: What does this agent actually read at the moment of action, and where is the policy enforced if not there?
concepts.evidence: Trace a task across the four functions, including external controls and feedback.
concepts.falsifier: Unmapped responsibilities or boundary failures show that the chosen decomposition is incomplete.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: These are functional planes, not a universal implementation standard or chronological stack.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 205; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
concepts.category: Intelligence systems and architecture · Enterprise processes, ownership and procurement

concepts.name: Context and Delegation Trust Boundaries
concepts.definition: A system's use of information and delegated actions requires explicit boundaries between instructions, untrusted content, credentials and authorized execution.
concepts.keyQuestion: Where are information provenance, permissions, delegated scope and external action controls enforced, and how are persistent memories handled?
concepts.use_when: Where are information provenance, permissions, delegated scope and external action controls enforced, and how are persistent memories handled?
concepts.evidence: Inspect trust labels, permission checks, external enforcement and adversarial task tests.
concepts.falsifier: Unauthorized action or untrusted content overriding authority refutes the claimed boundary effectiveness.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Models contain learned information beyond the context window; enforcement need not reside inside the model.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 206; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: The Attack Surface Is the Window

concepts.name: Query and Vocabulary Fit
concepts.definition: A knowledge store's representation and retrieval methods determine which human or agent questions it can answer accurately and efficiently; domain-approved vocabulary helps preserve business meaning.
concepts.keyQuestion: Is this store shaped for the question the agent asks, and did the business sign the vocabulary it uses?
concepts.use_when: Is this store shaped for the question the agent asks, and did the business sign the vocabulary it uses?
concepts.evidence: Compare key lookup, similarity, reference and graph traversal on representative queries; measure answer quality, latency and cost and obtain domain-owner review of the vocabulary.
concepts.falsifier: Equivalent performance from a simpler representation or domain disagreement about the encoded meaning weakens the proposed semantic design.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Humans and agents can use several query forms. Token-cost comparisons are workload-specific; a business-approved vocabulary is neither sufficient validation nor a requirement for a graph to be technically an ontology.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 207; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
concepts.category: Intelligence systems and architecture · Enterprise processes, ownership and procurement

concepts.name: Metric Optimization Pressure
concepts.definition: Optimizing a proxy can reduce its usefulness when behavior exploits the gap between the measure and the intended outcome.
concepts.keyQuestion: Can the thing being optimized see the measure I am using to judge it?
concepts.use_when: Can the thing being optimized see the measure I am using to judge it?
concepts.evidence: Compare proxy gains with independent outcome measures, adversarial cases and distribution shifts.
concepts.falsifier: Sustained outcome improvement on fresh cases weakens a metric-gaming explanation.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Goodhart effects, contamination, sycophancy and deceptive behavior are distinct hypotheses, not one physical law.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 208; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

applications.name: Growth Metrics and Real Outcomes
applications.definition: Growth optimization can reward activity that raises a proxy while failing to improve durable customer or economic outcomes.
applications.evidence: Compare activation or usage metrics with retention, contribution and independently accepted value.
applications.falsifier: Sustained improvements in those outcomes weaken a proxy-gaming diagnosis.
applications.limits: A disappointing business result need not imply intentional gaming.

concepts.name: Independent Evaluation Standard
concepts.definition: A system needs an outcome standard and evaluation process sufficiently independent of its optimization process to detect real failures.
concepts.keyQuestion: Is there a referee this loop cannot see, and was it frozen before the loop started?
concepts.use_when: Is there a referee this loop cannot see, and was it frozen before the loop started?
concepts.evidence: Use versioned holdouts, fresh cases, contamination checks, adversarial tests and live outcome monitoring.
concepts.falsifier: High suite performance with repeated live failure weakens the suite's validity.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: A frozen or secret suite alone is insufficient; independence is proportionate to risk and may include external review.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 209; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
concepts.category: Deployment, product economics and outcomes · Enterprise processes, ownership and procurement

concepts.name: Behavioral Acceptance Specification
concepts.definition: Specify observable acceptable behavior, failure handling and authority boundaries before treating a demonstration as successful delivery.
concepts.keyQuestion: Does this product have a specification a model can be graded against, and was the model chosen before or after it existed?
concepts.use_when: Does this product have a specification a model can be graded against, and was the model chosen before or after it existed?
concepts.evidence: Write representative cases, thresholds, exception paths and acceptance responsibilities before the proof.
concepts.falsifier: Repeated disagreement among qualified evaluators exposes an underspecified standard.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Requirements and feasibility co-evolve; model selection need not wait until the last week.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 210; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: Evaluation Is the Specification (The Model Chosen Last)

concepts.name: Governed Decision Loop
concepts.definition: Connect a stated outcome, evaluation standard, authorized execution and observed feedback in a repeatable loop with an accountable owner.
concepts.keyQuestion: Is this a loop the firm owns, or a person doing the loop's job by hand?
concepts.use_when: Is this a loop the firm owns, or a person doing the loop's job by hand?
concepts.evidence: Trace outcome, decision, action, evidence, exception and update for representative cases.
concepts.falsifier: Unowned exceptions or missing feedback break the claim of a governed loop.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Automation is optional; the loop can include human decisions and external controls.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 212; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
concepts.category: Deployment, product economics and outcomes · Organization, roles and expert work

concepts.name: Engineered Unit Economics
concepts.definition: Operational design can change unit cost through routing, caching, batching, retrieval, review and exception handling.
concepts.keyQuestion: Which of the four margin levers has this company pulled, and which is still available?
concepts.use_when: Which of the four margin levers has this company pulled, and which is still available?
concepts.evidence: Measure each intervention's incremental cost, accepted quality and realized volume against a baseline.
concepts.falsifier: Savings erased by maintenance, rework or quality loss weaken the margin-improvement thesis.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Available levers are not realized savings; report implementation costs and dates.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 213; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: Gross Margin as a Design Outcome

concepts.name: Usage-Tail Pricing
concepts.definition: Heavy or difficult usage can dominate service cost, making average-user economics an unreliable pricing guide.
concepts.keyQuestion: Does this price track the work done and the tail that does it, or the chairs?
concepts.use_when: Does this price track the work done and the tail that does it, or the chairs?
concepts.evidence: Model the cost distribution, correlated peaks, retries and cohort contribution rather than only the mean.
concepts.falsifier: Thin stable tails and predictable usage weaken the case for special tail controls.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Caps and pricing changes can reduce customer value; test incentives and fairness of the chosen unit.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 214; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: Pricing as a Finance Instrument (Price the Tail)

concepts.name: Hybrid Pricing Transition
concepts.definition: Combine subscription, usage and outcome-linked charges when measurement, attribution and risk allocation support different units at different stages.
concepts.keyQuestion: Which rung of the seat-to-outcome ramp is this contract on, and who is carrying the guarantee's cost?
concepts.use_when: Which rung of the seat-to-outcome ramp is this contract on, and who is carrying the guarantee's cost?
concepts.evidence: Test buyer acceptance, margin volatility, attribution disputes and incentives under each pricing mix.
concepts.falsifier: Stable economics and incentives in a hybrid can refute the need to reach pure outcome pricing.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Outcome pricing is a possible design, not an inevitable end state.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 215; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: Outcome Pricing Is an End State (The Hybrid Is the Transition)

concepts.name: Valuation Assumption Audit
concepts.definition: Build a valuation from reconciled revenue, cost, durability, control, funding and failure assumptions before using a market multiple as a cross-check.
concepts.keyQuestion: Which of the five assumptions is this valuation still making, and in which direction does the error run?
concepts.use_when: Which of the five assumptions is this valuation still making, and in which direction does the error run?
concepts.evidence: Document a cash-flow bridge, competing valuation and sensitivity to the assumptions that explain the gap.
concepts.falsifier: An unresolved counting or cash-flow inconsistency invalidates precision in the headline value.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: The nine-question order is a practical workflow, not the only valid valuation method.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 220; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: The Multiple Comes Last (The Five Broken Assumptions)

concepts.name: Revenue Counting Boundary
concepts.definition: Define whether the analysis counts reported company revenue, gross transactions or final-customer demand, then reconcile the chosen boundary.
concepts.keyQuestion: What is this company's counted top line, and what is the ratio of counted to reported?
concepts.use_when: What is this company's counted top line, and what is the ratio of counted to reported?
concepts.evidence: Bridge tiers, payer classes, gross versus net treatment and run-rate versus realized annual revenue.
concepts.falsifier: A boundary-consistent bridge can refute an apparent overstatement caused only by unlike measures.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Partner-funded revenue may be recognized legitimately; demand independence is a separate analysis.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 221; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Durable and Perishable Value
concepts.definition: Separate cash flows supported by persistent assets and relationships from those exposed to likely substitution or rapid decay.
concepts.keyQuestion: What fraction of this company survives the next release, and is the multiple being applied to that fraction or to the whole?
concepts.use_when: What fraction of this company survives the next release, and is the multiple being applied to that fraction or to the whole?
concepts.evidence: Model renewal, switching, replacement and reinvestment under explicit durability scenarios.
concepts.falsifier: Durable retention despite anticipated substitution weakens the assumed decay rate.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Durability is a spectrum; terminal value also depends on reinvestment, competition and sustainable growth.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 222; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Enterprise Value and Obligation Reconciliation
concepts.definition: Reconcile operating value with equity and other claims, cash and non-operating assets, and separately identified contingent or debt-like exposures.
concepts.keyQuestion: Which claims, non-operating assets and contingent obligations reconcile operating value to equity value without double counting?
concepts.use_when: Which claims, non-operating assets and contingent obligations reconcile operating value to equity value without double counting?
concepts.evidence: Bridge equity, debt, preferred claims, noncontrolling interests and relevant cash with consistent DCF and lease treatment.
concepts.falsifier: An obligation already included in cash flows or debt exposes double counting if added again.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Not every purchase commitment is debt; avoid subtracting cash or adding liabilities twice.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 223; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: The EV Bridge With Hidden Piers

concepts.name: Failure Scenario Valuation
concepts.definition: Identify mechanisms that can destroy or sharply reduce equity value and model their triggers, timing, recovery and probability where supportable.
concepts.keyQuestion: What kills this company, what is the trigger, and what is the probability-weighted value once that case is in the sum?
concepts.use_when: What kills this company, what is the trigger, and what is the probability-weighted value once that case is in the sum?
concepts.evidence: Stress liquidity, substitution, concentration and asset recovery with explicit correlated assumptions.
concepts.falsifier: Adequate recovery or resilient cash flow can refute a literal worthless scenario.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Three cases is a drafting aid; probabilities must be supported and scenarios must not be double counted.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 224; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Transaction Perimeter Read
concepts.definition: A transaction price is interpretable only after identifying the assets, liabilities, rights, control and contingencies actually transferred.
concepts.keyQuestion: In this deal, what did the buyer pay for and what did it leave behind, and what does that say about the residual of the whole company?
concepts.use_when: In this deal, what did the buyer pay for and what did it leave behind, and what does that say about the residual of the whole company?
concepts.evidence: Read the deal perimeter, consideration, assumed debt, earnouts and retained obligations.
concepts.falsifier: Material excluded assets or contingent payments undermine a simple headline-price comparison.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: An announced valuation is not always cash consideration or enterprise value.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 226; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Buyer and Seller Repetition Asymmetry
concepts.definition: A repeat seller may possess more information and process experience than an occasional buyer, affecting negotiation and evaluation quality.
concepts.keyQuestion: What instrument does this buyer hold that substitutes for the repetitions the seller has and it does not?
concepts.use_when: What instrument does this buyer hold that substitutes for the repetitions the seller has and it does not?
concepts.evidence: Compare access to benchmarks, reference cases, contract expertise and independent verification.
concepts.falsifier: An experienced buyer with credible alternatives can reverse the presumed asymmetry.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Do not infer bad faith from experience; design the process to reduce information gaps.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 229; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Buyer Qualification Framework
concepts.definition: Evaluate verification, economics, rights, incentives, feasibility, independence, exposure and drift before and during a supplier relationship.
concepts.keyQuestion: Which letters of VERIFIED hold an artifact, and which is the one nobody checked?
concepts.use_when: Which letters of VERIFIED hold an artifact, and which is the one nobody checked?
concepts.evidence: Require a named owner, dated artifact and disposition for each VERIFIED step.
concepts.falsifier: Missing artifacts or failed mandatory gates refute a claim of completed qualification.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Price can compensate some commercial risks, but cannot cure absent required authority or a non-negotiable safety or legal gate.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 230; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Evaluation Provenance and Buyer Control
concepts.definition: Determine who selected, prepared and scored evaluation cases and which conditions differ from real buyer use.
concepts.keyQuestion: Which part of this evaluation could the vendor have staged, and which part ran on my floor against my referee?
concepts.use_when: Which part of this evaluation could the vendor have staged, and which part ran on my floor against my referee?
concepts.evidence: Run buyer-controlled cases on representative systems with staged and unstaged conditions separated.
concepts.falsifier: Comparable results on fresh buyer cases weaken a procurement-theater concern.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Vendor involvement can be useful; disclose it and preserve independent acceptance authority.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 231; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Governed Fast Intake
concepts.definition: Provide a rapid, visible path for evaluating and approving tools so that governance does not simply drive work into unobserved channels.
concepts.keyQuestion: Can this firm say yes in days while keeping clear title to what the purchase will compound?
concepts.use_when: Can this firm say yes in days while keeping clear title to what the purchase will compound?
concepts.evidence: Measure intake time, shadow usage, incidents, adoption and coverage of approved paths.
concepts.falsifier: Long queues with continued shadow use refute the claim of effective governed intake.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Speed cannot waive mandatory authorization, security or legal requirements.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 232; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Deployment Control Inheritance
concepts.definition: Defaults chosen during implementation can become durable control points over identity, data, evaluation, workflows and future change.
concepts.keyQuestion: Who wired this loop, and whose walls does its exhaust accumulate inside?
concepts.use_when: Who wired this loop, and whose walls does its exhaust accumulate inside?
concepts.evidence: Inventory deployed accounts, ownership, permissions, repositories, standards and export paths at handover.
concepts.falsifier: Buyer-controlled configuration and rehearsed migration weaken the inherited-capture thesis.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Initial convenience does not establish permanent dependence; contracts and technical transfer both matter.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 234; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: The Hand That Wires the Harness Chooses the Landlord

concepts.name: Subsidy and Substitution Timing
concepts.definition: A subsidy can accelerate adoption before dependency forms, while later substitution or repricing changes the relationship's economics.
concepts.keyQuestion: Which hinge is this firm timing against, the subsidy that expires or the feasibility that does not?
concepts.use_when: Which hinge is this firm timing against, the subsidy that expires or the feasibility that does not?
concepts.evidence: Compare subsidy expiry, integration milestones, available alternatives and repricing rights.
concepts.falsifier: Portable deployments and sustained competitive pricing weaken a delayed-capture hypothesis.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Introductory discounts are not proof of an intended lock-in strategy.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 235; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Portability-Aligned Delivery
concepts.definition: A service provider can create value by leaving the client with usable artifacts, skills and a priced exit rather than maximizing dependence.
concepts.keyQuestion: Does this engagement leave the enterprise able to migrate in six weeks, and who gets paid when it can?
concepts.use_when: Does this engagement leave the enterprise able to migrate in six weeks, and who gets paid when it can?
concepts.evidence: Inspect retained artifacts, client competence, recurring support needs and exercised alternate execution.
concepts.falsifier: A technically documented exit requiring a practical rebuild weakens the independence claim.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Independence has maintenance costs; a services relationship can remain economically sensible.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 236; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Layered Dependency Audit
concepts.definition: Assess dependency separately in data, semantics, runtime, model, control, commercial terms and operating skills.
concepts.keyQuestion: In which of the three cages is this enterprise, and is the sovereignty it was sold the customer's or the vendor's?
concepts.use_when: In which of the three cages is this enterprise, and is the sovereignty it was sold the customer's or the vendor's?
concepts.evidence: Perform a workload-specific exit and replacement inventory with rights, costs and timing per layer.
concepts.falsifier: Successful transfer of one layer does not refute dependence elsewhere; a complete alternative path does.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Open source at one layer does not make the whole system independent.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 237; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Enterprise as Distribution Complement
concepts.definition: An enterprise can supply demand, workflow access and trusted distribution that help a technology provider commercialize a capability.
concepts.keyQuestion: Which vendor's silicon does this enterprise stack distribute, and who wrapped it into something buyable?
concepts.use_when: Which vendor's silicon does this enterprise stack distribute, and who wrapped it into something buyable?
concepts.evidence: Trace the provider's incremental reach, conversion and retained control through the enterprise relationship.
concepts.falsifier: Little incremental demand or readily substitutable access weakens the distribution-complement thesis.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: The enterprise may capture substantial value too; dependence must be assessed in both directions.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 238; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Relative Productivity Advantage
concepts.definition: An absolute productivity gain does not ensure competitive advantage if peers gain similarly or customers capture the savings.
concepts.keyQuestion: Your people are faster. Is the firm ahead, and by what asymmetry?
concepts.use_when: Your people are faster. Is the firm ahead, and by what asymmetry?
concepts.evidence: Compare quality-adjusted throughput, cost, price and share against a relevant peer or counterfactual.
concepts.falsifier: Durable relative improvement and retained margin can support an advantage beyond a neutral gain.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Industry-wide gains can still benefit customers and workers without creating excess firm profits.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 239; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
concepts.category: Organization, roles and expert work · Strategy, competition and value capture

concepts.name: Productivity Transmission Across Scales
concepts.definition: Task gains affect firm performance only when workflow, organizational and business-model constraints allow the gains to propagate.
concepts.keyQuestion: At which scale did this firm's gain stop climbing, and what would carry it one level up?
concepts.use_when: At which scale did this firm's gain stop climbing, and what would carry it one level up?
concepts.evidence: Measure task time, end-to-end throughput, operating outcomes and economic capture on aligned dates.
concepts.falsifier: A task improvement with no downstream change identifies a broken transmission link.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Task, workflow, firm and market are analytical scales, not a mandatory maturity sequence.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 240; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Federated Discovery and Central Coordination
concepts.definition: Local experimentation can coexist with shared standards, reusable infrastructure and explicit responsibility for common constraints.
concepts.keyQuestion: What is this firm's conversion time from an edge discovery to a governed loop, and who owns the paved road?
concepts.use_when: What is this firm's conversion time from an edge discovery to a governed loop, and who owns the paved road?
concepts.evidence: Compare discovery speed, duplication, paved-path use, exceptions and cross-team reuse.
concepts.falsifier: Central delay or uncontrolled fragmentation can refute the chosen balance.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: The appropriate center varies with risk, heterogeneity, scale and capabilities.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 241; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: Edges Find and Cannot Choose; Center Chooses and Cannot Find

concepts.name: Complementary Organizational Change
concepts.definition: Technology creates more value when workflows, incentives, skills and decision rights are adapted to use it effectively.
concepts.keyQuestion: Has this firm installed the technology or rebuilt the floor around what it makes cheap?
concepts.use_when: Has this firm installed the technology or rebuilt the floor around what it makes cheap?
concepts.evidence: Compare similar deployments with different complementary changes and account for selection effects.
concepts.falsifier: Equal outcomes without the proposed complement weaken its claimed necessity.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Complementarity does not imply that every organization needs a full reorganization first.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 242; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: Installation Is the Entry Fee, Reorganization Is the Harvest

concepts.name: Task Automation and Augmentation
concepts.definition: Analyze which tasks can be automated, assisted or redesigned while distinguishing task changes from whole-job outcomes.
concepts.keyQuestion: On this task line, which spans are automated, which enhanced, and where does the next person enter?
concepts.use_when: On this task line, which spans are automated, which enhanced, and where does the next person enter?
concepts.evidence: Observe quality, demand, new tasks, supervision and labor allocation before and after adoption.
concepts.falsifier: Persisting expert requirements or expanded demand can overturn simple replacement forecasts.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: A task capability demonstration is not a headcount prediction.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 243; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: Automation or Enhancement Is a Deployment Choice

concepts.name: Human and Agent Capacity Envelope
concepts.definition: Set a team's span of agent-supported work according to measured quality, exception load, supervision and accountability.
concepts.keyQuestion: Is this ratio backed by a measured gate, and at what ratio did the gate last bend?
concepts.use_when: Is this ratio backed by a measured gate, and at what ratio did the gate last bend?
concepts.evidence: Measure accepted throughput, incidents, adjudication burden and response capacity before changing ratios.
concepts.falsifier: Rising unresolved exceptions or quality loss refutes a claimed safe expansion of span.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: No universal human-to-agent ratio is supplied; headcount alone is not a performance gauge.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 244; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: The Ratio Rule (Push Until the Gate Bends)

concepts.name: Organizational Complementarity Moat
concepts.definition: Residue, a deliberate ownership boundary, coordination capital and default status with machine buyers are four proposed sources of organizational advantage that may reinforce one another.
concepts.keyQuestion: Which of residue, ownership, coordination and buyer preference produces measurable advantage, and how do the mechanisms interact?
concepts.use_when: Which of residue, ownership, coordination and buyer preference produces measurable advantage, and how do the mechanisms interact?
concepts.evidence: Measure usable learning, exercised control and exit, coordinated throughput, buyer selection and the difficulty of replicating their combination.
concepts.falsifier: Easy replication, unused residue, expensive control or no buyer preference weakens the moat claim.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: The proposed cost-to-speed-to-optionality-to-moat sequence is not a strict law; verify the links and account for complexity and maintenance.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 246; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
concepts.category: Organization, roles and expert work · Strategy, competition and value capture

concepts.name: Apprenticeship Erosion and Redesign
concepts.definition: Automating routine work can remove the practice through which newcomers developed judgment, requiring a deliberate replacement learning path.
concepts.keyQuestion: Where in this firm is judgment being built now that the stairs are gone, and is it enforced by structure or by exhortation?
concepts.use_when: Where in this firm is judgment being built now that the stairs are gone, and is it enforced by structure or by exhortation?
concepts.evidence: Track exposure to cases, feedback quality, error correction and independent competence over time.
concepts.falsifier: Equivalent skill development through existing paths weakens the claim that the first rung is missing.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Ninety days is a configurable program target, not a validated universal time to competence.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 247; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

applications.name: Moving the Entry Point
applications.definition: Redesign junior entry roles around supervised operation, evaluation and learning when routine production tasks are automated.
applications.evidence: Assess case-based learning, demonstrated judgment and opportunities to progress beyond tool operation.
applications.falsifier: Strong existing apprenticeship outcomes weaken the need to replace the entry path.
applications.limits: Automation can both remove and create jobs; no universal employment direction follows.

concepts.name: Exception Judgment and Standard Evolution
concepts.definition: Experts can create lasting value by resolving novel exceptions and converting justified decisions into improved standards.
concepts.keyQuestion: Who in this firm can say what the standard should be when it is silent, and does each of their judgments become a case?
concepts.use_when: Who in this firm can say what the standard should be when it is silent, and does each of their judgments become a case?
concepts.evidence: Trace exceptions through adjudication, rationale, standard changes and recurrence reduction.
concepts.falsifier: Unchanged standards or repeated failures weaken a claim that expert judgment is compounding.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Not every exception should become a rule; preserve context and dissent where uncertainty remains.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 248; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Expert Seeding Investment
concepts.definition: Expert-designed examples and acceptance cases can provide initial structure for a system before operating feedback is available.
concepts.keyQuestion: Who seeded this loop, how many cases did they adjudicate, and did they sign the vocabulary?
concepts.use_when: Who seeded this loop, how many cases did they adjudicate, and did they sign the vocabulary?
concepts.evidence: Measure coverage, inter-rater agreement, held-out performance and the value of additional cases.
concepts.falsifier: Poor transfer to fresh cases weakens the seed set's usefulness.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: A target such as fifty seed cases is illustrative; diversity and difficulty matter more than a fixed count.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 249; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Expert Leverage Economics
concepts.definition: An expert can support more valuable work through reusable knowledge and governed execution when review and exception burdens remain manageable.
concepts.keyQuestion: How many loops does each senior in this firm sign, and is the price attached to the outcome or the hour?
concepts.use_when: How many loops does each senior in this firm sign, and is the price attached to the outcome or the hour?
concepts.evidence: Compare accepted outcomes, quality, review time, total cost and client value across increasing scope.
concepts.falsifier: Rising rework or diluted judgment can erase the apparent leverage.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Revenue per employee alone omits capital, contractors, pricing and quality.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 250; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Four Ownerships of AI Work
concepts.definition: Assign accountability for the substrate, the junctions, the acceptance standard and the exit, with budget authority and the right to stop where necessary.
concepts.keyQuestion: Who is accountable for the substrate, the junctions, the standard and the exit, with what budget and stop authority?
concepts.use_when: Who is accountable for the substrate, the junctions, the standard and the exit, with what budget and stop authority?
concepts.evidence: Name the decision right, owner, escalation and supporting artifacts for each ownership.
concepts.falsifier: Conflicting owners or unowned decisions refute a complete accountability design.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: These are rights and responsibilities, not four mandatory executive titles.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 251; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
concepts.category: Organization, roles and expert work · Enterprise processes, ownership and procurement

concepts.name: Executive Role Reconfiguration
concepts.definition: AI responsibilities can be absorbed by an incumbent role, displace its remit, or converge with another role; a new seat is useful only when the ownership and authority gaps are resolved.
concepts.keyQuestion: Is this new title going to be absorbed, displace the seat, or converge with it, and which of the four ownerships decides?
concepts.use_when: Is this new title going to be absorbed, displace the seat, or converge with it, and which of the four ownerships decides?
concepts.evidence: Map the four ownerships and actual authority before comparing title options.
concepts.falsifier: A new title without resolved authority or capability weakens a reorganization claim.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: No particular executive title is a universal solution.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 252; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Deployment Decision Sequence
concepts.definition: Move an engagement through Discovery, Envelope, Proof, Landing, Outcome and Yield with dated decisions, evidence and accountable owners.
concepts.keyQuestion: Which letter of DEPLOY is this engagement on, what is its date, and what did the architect refuse in writing?
concepts.use_when: Which letter of DEPLOY is this engagement on, what is its date, and what did the architect refuse in writing?
concepts.evidence: Track entry evidence, acceptance, constraints, refusal reasons and transition dates for each stage.
concepts.falsifier: Missing baselines or unsigned operating responsibility refute a claimed completed deployment.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: The source's four discovery gates and seven-layer shape need explicit local definitions; model feasibility should be tested early.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 256; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: The CTO of Someone Else's Company (DEPLOY)

concepts.name: Intent-Based Monetization
concepts.definition: A service can monetize information about a user's likely purchase or action when it improves matching, conversion or transaction value.
concepts.keyQuestion: Which of this business's margin assumptions rests on the copy being free, and does the copy still cost nothing?
concepts.use_when: Which of this business's margin assumptions rests on the copy being free, and does the copy still cost nothing?
concepts.evidence: Measure incremental conversion, auction or pricing economics, privacy constraints and substitution.
concepts.falsifier: Low incremental value or cheaper equivalent matching weakens the intent-rent thesis.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Intent is one scarce input among others; avoid universal profitability or zero-copy-cost claims.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 260; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.
aliases: Intent Is the Scarcest Thing on the Web

concepts.name: Transformation Direction
concepts.definition: Technology can change distribution, operations and the business model in different sequences depending on existing infrastructure and incentives.
concepts.keyQuestion: Is this transformation being attempted from the outside in, when the era runs from the inside out?
concepts.use_when: Is this transformation being attempted from the outside in, when the era runs from the inside out?
concepts.evidence: Date changes in workflows, economics and distribution, then compare plausible alternative sequences.
concepts.falsifier: Distribution-led AI change or operations-led web change refutes a universal era-specific sequence.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Outside-in and inside-out are contingent patterns, not historical laws or required branding.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 261; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Dual-Surface Product Design
concepts.definition: A product can expose a human interface and an agent specification or API over consistent business rules, permissions and state, evaluated against a shared outcome standard.
concepts.keyQuestion: Does this product have an agent surface, and is it graded by the same referee as the human one?
concepts.use_when: Does this product have an agent surface, and is it graded by the same referee as the human one?
concepts.evidence: Run representative tasks through both surfaces and compare accepted outcomes, authorization, state changes and exception handling.
concepts.falsifier: Divergent business rules or success on the screen with failure through the machine interface weakens the shared-product claim.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: The surfaces need not expose identical capabilities or workflows; define activation and retention in terms of actual accepted value where useful.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 218; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

concepts.name: Decision Residue Flywheel
concepts.definition: Operational traces, adjudicated cases, evaluation results and configuration changes can improve subsequent work when permitted capture, curation and a tested learning process turn them into reusable assets.
concepts.keyQuestion: Where does this deployment's exhaust accumulate, and whose walls is it inside?
concepts.use_when: Where does this deployment's exhaust accumulate, and whose walls is it inside?
concepts.evidence: Follow traces into curated cases, system changes, reuse and measured improvement across comparable decisions; identify who controls and benefits from each step.
concepts.falsifier: Growing records without better performance, lower rework or practical reuse weakens the flywheel claim.
concepts.decision: Use the observed result to accept, modify or reject the intervention or valuation implied by this mechanism.
concepts.limits: Provider training on customer data depends on contracts and settings. An open harness does not by itself guarantee retained rights, privacy or learning.
concepts.origin: Reconciled from expansion pack entry 194; supplied source is not independent empirical validation.

applications.name: Residue as a Second Output
applications.definition: A successful work loop can deliver the immediate outcome and reusable evidence that improves later execution.
applications.evidence: Measure artifact capture, curation, ownership, reuse and downstream performance separately.
applications.falsifier: High capture without reuse or benefit weakens a compounding claim.
applications.limits: The useful capture rate depends on task, privacy, consent and maintenance economics.
